questions.subject: maths
questions.question: What is the value of 24 x 15?

questions.subject: maths
questions.question: Which of the following is a prime number?
questions.explanation: 29 is only divisible by 1 and itself, making it prime. 21=3x7, 27=3x9, 35=5x7.

questions.subject: maths
questions.question: If a triangle has angles 60 degrees and 80 degrees, what is the third angle?
questions.explanation: Sum of all angles in a triangle = 180 degrees. Third angle = 180 - 60 - 80 = 40 degrees.

questions.subject: maths
questions.question: If 2x + 5 = 17, what is x?

questions.subject: maths
questions.question: What is the square root of 144?

questions.subject: maths
questions.question: What is the area of a circle with radius 7 cm? (use pi = 22/7)

questions.subject: maths
questions.question: The sum of first 10 natural numbers is:
questions.explanation: Sum of first n natural numbers = n(n+1)/2 = 10 x 11 / 2 = 55.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which gas do plants absorb from the atmosphere during photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Plants absorb Carbon Dioxide (CO2) from the air and use sunlight and water to make food (glucose) through photosynthesis.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which organ of the body purifies blood?
questions.explanation: The kidneys filter waste products and excess water from the blood to produce urine. They are the main blood purifiers.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the unit of electric current?
questions.explanation: Electric current is measured in Amperes (A), named after French physicist Andre-Marie Ampere.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: An object travels 60 metres in 4 seconds. What is its speed?
questions.explanation: Speed = Distance / Time = 60 / 4 = 15 m/s.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: What is the SI unit of force?
questions.explanation: Force is measured in Newtons (N), named after Sir Isaac Newton. F = ma.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: What is the chemical formula of water?
questions.explanation: Water is composed of 2 Hydrogen atoms and 1 Oxygen atom, giving it the formula H2O.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Baking soda is the common name for:
questions.explanation: Baking soda is sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO3). It is used in cooking and as an antacid.

questions.subject: biology
questions.question: Which organelle is called the powerhouse of the cell?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria produce ATP (energy) through cellular respiration, earning the nickname powerhouse of the cell.

questions.subject: biology
questions.question: Which blood group is called the universal donor?
questions.explanation: Blood group O negative can donate to all other blood groups, making it the universal donor.

questions.subject: history
questions.question: The Indus Valley Civilization was located mainly in which present-day countries?
questions.explanation: The Indus Valley Civilization (also called Harappan Civilization) flourished mainly in the area that is now India and Pakistan.

questions.subject: history
questions.question: Who built the Taj Mahal?
questions.explanation: The Taj Mahal was built by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal. Construction was completed in 1653.

questions.subject: history
questions.question: The Battle of Plassey was fought in which year?
questions.explanation: The Battle of Plassey was fought on June 23, 1757 between the British East India Company and the Nawab of Bengal, marking the beginning of British rule in India.

questions.subject: history
questions.question: Who was the founder of the Maurya Empire?
questions.explanation: Chandragupta Maurya founded the Maurya Empire around 321 BCE with the guidance of Chanakya (Kautilya).

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: Which is the longest river in India?
questions.explanation: The Ganga is the longest river in India, stretching approximately 2,525 km from the Gangotri Glacier to the Bay of Bengal.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: Which is the highest mountain peak in India?
questions.explanation: Kangchenjunga (8,586 m) is the highest mountain peak entirely within Indian territory, located on the India-Nepal border in Sikkim.

questions.subject: civics
questions.question: India became a Republic on:
questions.explanation: India became a Republic on 26 January 1950 when the Constitution of India came into effect. This is why we celebrate Republic Day on January 26.

questions.subject: civics
questions.question: How many Fundamental Rights are guaranteed by the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: The Indian Constitution guarantees 6 Fundamental Rights: Right to Equality, Right to Freedom, Right against Exploitation, Right to Freedom of Religion, Cultural and Educational Rights, and Right to Constitutional Remedies.

questions.subject: civics
questions.question: Who is the constitutional head of the Indian state?
questions.explanation: The President of India is the constitutional head of state. The Prime Minister is the head of government.

questions.subject: current_affairs
questions.question: Which Indian city is known as the Silicon Valley of India?
questions.explanation: Bengaluru (Bangalore) is called the Silicon Valley of India due to its large concentration of IT companies and startups.

questions.subject: current_affairs
questions.question: India's national animal is the:
questions.explanation: The Bengal Tiger (Panthera tigris tigris) is India's national animal. Project Tiger was launched in 1973 to protect tigers.

questions.subject: current_affairs
questions.question: ISRO stands for:
questions.explanation: ISRO - Indian Space Research Organisation - is India's national space agency, headquartered in Bengaluru, founded in 1969.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Rusting of iron is an example of which type of change?
questions.explanation: Rusting is a chemical change because iron reacts with oxygen and water to form iron oxide (rust), which cannot be easily reversed.

questions.subject: maths
questions.question: What fraction is equivalent to 3/4?
questions.explanation: 9/12 = (9 / 3) / (12 / 3) = 3/4. Multiply both numerator and denominator of 3/4 by 3 to get 9/12.

questions.subject: history
questions.question: The Indian National Congress was founded in which year?
questions.explanation: The Indian National Congress was founded on 28 December 1885 by Allan Octavian Hume, Dadabhai Naoroji, and Dinshaw Wacha.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: The Thar Desert is located in which Indian state?
questions.explanation: The Thar Desert (Great Indian Desert) is primarily located in the Indian state of Rajasthan, extending into Pakistan.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
questions.explanation: Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun, at an average distance of about 57.9 million kilometres.

questions.subject: maths
questions.question: The value of sin 90 degrees is:
questions.explanation: sin 90 degrees = 1. This is a fundamental trigonometric value. The unit circle shows the y-coordinate is 1 at 90 degrees.

questions.subject: biology
questions.question: Which vitamin is produced in the human body when exposed to sunlight?
questions.explanation: Vitamin D is synthesized in the skin when it is exposed to ultraviolet rays from sunlight.

questions.subject: civics
questions.question: Panchayati Raj is related to:
questions.explanation: Panchayati Raj is a system of governance in which local self-government for rural areas is established through elected bodies called Panchayats.

questions.subject: current_affairs
questions.question: Chandrayaan-3 made India the first country to land near the Moon's south pole. In which year did this happen?
questions.explanation: Chandrayaan-3 successfully landed near the lunar south pole on August 23, 2023. India became the first country to achieve this feat.

questions.subject: history
questions.question: The Non-Cooperation Movement was launched by Mahatma Gandhi in which year?
questions.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi launched the Non-Cooperation Movement in 1920 in response to the Jallianwala Bagh massacre and the Khilafat issue.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: According to Ohm's Law, if voltage is 12V and resistance is 4 Ohms, what is the current?
questions.explanation: Ohm's Law: V = IR. Current I = V/R = 12/4 = 3 Amperes.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: The pH of a neutral solution at 25 degrees Celsius is:
questions.explanation: A neutral solution (like pure water) has a pH of exactly 7 at 25 degrees Celsius. Below 7 is acidic, above 7 is basic.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: The Sundarbans mangrove forest is shared between India and which other country?
questions.explanation: The Sundarbans is the world's largest mangrove forest, shared between India (West Bengal) and Bangladesh. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

questions.subject: maths
questions.question: The product of two consecutive even numbers is 168. What are the numbers?

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which gas is commonly used in fire extinguishers?
questions.explanation: Carbon Dioxide (CO2) is used in fire extinguishers because it does not support combustion and is heavier than air, smothering the fire.

questions.subject: biology
questions.question: DNA replication occurs during which phase of the cell cycle?
questions.explanation: DNA replication (synthesis) occurs during the S (Synthesis) phase of interphase in the cell cycle.

questions.subject: civics
questions.question: The Right to Education Act (RTE) guarantees free and compulsory education up to which age?
questions.explanation: The Right to Education (RTE) Act 2009 guarantees free and compulsory education to all children between the ages of 6 and 14 years.

questions.subject: current_affairs
questions.question: What is the capital of India?
questions.explanation: New Delhi is the capital city of India and the seat of all three branches of the Government of India.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A ball is dropped from a height. Which energy conversion takes place?
questions.explanation: As the ball falls, its Potential Energy (due to height) converts to Kinetic Energy (due to motion).

questions.subject: history
questions.question: The Dandi March was a protest against which British law?
questions.explanation: The Dandi March (Salt March) in 1930 was led by Mahatma Gandhi to protest the British monopoly on salt production and the salt tax.

questions.subject: maths
questions.question: If A = {1,2,3} and B = {2,3,4}, what is A union B?
questions.explanation: A union B contains all elements that are in A or in B (or both): {1,2,3} + {4} = {1,2,3,4}.
